title: WannierSTM: Efficient superconducting scanning-probe spectroscopy from maximally localized Wannier functions
authors: Oscar Moreno Segura, Dorye L. Esteras, Andrei Shumilin, Gonzalo Rivero-Carracedo, Riku Tuovinen, José J. Baldoví
abstract: We present a Python-based program that combines maximally localized Wannier functions-based first-principles electronic structure with the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism to enable efficient simulations of scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The workflow builds upon standard density functional theory packages to construct compact transport Hamiltonians that preserve the properties of realistic materials. Superconductivity is incorporated via an effective pairing potential within the Nambu-spinor formalism, while coupling to the STM tip and substrate electrodes is treated using the wide-band limit approximation. Within this formulation, transport quantities such as current-voltage characteristics and differential conductance are evaluated in a closed analytical form. This avoids explicit numerical energy integrations and enables rapid spectroscopic calculations over broad parameter spaces. The framework provides a unified and computationally efficient approach for modeling superconducting hybrid nanostructures with spin-orbit coupling, magnetic textures, and spin polarization. Representative applications in spin chains, two-dimensional and molecular magnets on a superconductor demonstrate its robust capabilities for both simple model systems and realistic ab initio molecular structures relevant to modern STM experiments.
summary: This paper presents WannierSTM, a novel Python framework that efficiently simulates superconducting STM spectroscopy. It merges first-principles electronic structure (via MLWF) with the NEGF formalism to calculate transport properties. This allows for rapid, large-scale mapping of complex superconducting and magnetic phenomena at the atomic scale.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational challenge of simulating superconducting scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) spectroscopy using first-principles methods.
main_result: It introduces WannierSTM, a unified and computationally efficient Python framework for rapid spectroscopic calculations in superconducting hybrid nanostructures.
method: The method combines maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWF) derived from DFT with the Nonequilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) formalism.
model_or_system: The model simulates an open quantum system consisting of a central superconducting region coupled to STM tip and substrate electrodes. Superconductivity is incorporated via an effective pairing potential in the Nambu-spinor formalism.
key_observables: Current-voltage characteristics (I-V) and differential conductance (dI/dV) spectra.
important_parameters: Low-bias STM/STS regimes; systems exhibiting spin-orbit coupling, magnetic textures, and spin polarization.
main_assumptions: The calculation uses the wide-band limit approximation for electrode coupling and treats superconductivity at a mean-field level without self-consistent feedback from non-equilibrium currents.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the transport setup, showing the central region coupled to two electrodes (L and R).
paper_structure: The paper builds a theoretical framework by combining MLWF-based Hamiltonians with NEGF theory. It derives transport quantities analytically, avoiding explicit energy integrations, and demonstrates its application to various superconducting and magnetic systems.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a powerful, efficient tool for simulating open quantum systems (the STM junction) in superconducting regimes, bridging complex many-body physics with practical computational methods.
